laws.rule: Any watercraft brought into Wyoming from 1 March to 30 November must be inspected for aquatic invasive species (zebra and quagga mussels and other pests carried on boats) before it is launched; at other times, inspection is needed if it has been on mussel-infested water in the last 30 days. Everyone transporting watercraft, including rafts, canoes, kayaks, paddle boards and inflatables, must stop at any open check station on their route, even with a seal from an earlier inspection. Watercraft also need an AIS decal before launching, except inflatables under 10 feet (about 3 m) and paddle boards; a decal does not replace the inspection.
laws.penalty_signal: Nonresident decal: US$30 motorised, US$15 non-motorised (about A$43 and A$21 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040).

items.text: Since 1 July 2024 (Senate File 32, 2024), Wyoming bans adding synthetic substances to hemp and selling hemp or hemp products with more than 0.3% THC or other psychoactive substances, including psychoactive analogues and isomers of THC. Delta-8 THC is listed as a Schedule I controlled substance, alongside the THC that occurs naturally in cannabis. Breaking the hemp rules is a misdemeanour.

culture-cycles.note: Juneteenth and Columbus Day are not on the closure list. Saturday holidays close the Friday before; Sunday holidays close the Monday after. Federal holidays are on the United States record.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Devils Tower is a sacred site for American Indians. The National Park Service asks climbers not to climb in June, a culturally significant month for ceremonies.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: The June closure is voluntary, set in the 1995 Climbing Management Plan and kept in the 2006 update.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: National Park Service (Devils Tower National Monument); associated American Indian tribes.

layers.process: A backcountry permit is required year-round for overnight stays; day hiking needs none. Early-access lottery applications 1 to 20 March, notification about 25 March, early access 1 to about 25 April, general access from 26 April for 15 May to 31 October, and from 6 October for 1 November to 14 May. The page gives no years; confirm. Fees: US$10 lottery application (non-refundable), US$5 per person per night, US$10 per reservation (about A$14, A$7 and A$14). Online reservations at least three days ahead; walk-up permits in person up to two days before in summer. Central Backcountry Office 307-344-2160. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
